name: Geranium and poppy petal lip stain

image.caption: Geranium and poppy petal lip stain

lead: Before commercial lipstick, people coloured their lips at home with plant material, and red petals are a classic source. Geranium and poppy petals are the ones named in this home recipe.
The payoff is a sheer flush of pink or red on the lips without a store-bought product. No clinical research has tested petal stains specifically.

paras: Described in general terms, petals are crushed or steeped and the colour is dabbed onto the lips, sometimes with a balm or wax to hold it. Colour is typically sheer and fades with eating and time.
Plant pigments can cause irritation or allergy in some people, and homemade preparations are not regulated cosmetics. Anyone with plant allergies may react.

angle.text: The stain adds a sheer wash of colour to the lips, evening out pale lips with a natural-looking flush.

lead: Geranium and poppy petal lip stain is a historical, homemade way of tinting the lips using red flower petals.

Home-made lip colour pre-dates commercial sticks: before Guerlain's 1884 lipstick, lipstick was made at home, and 16th-century English recipes blended beeswax with red plant stains.[1] The petal stain belongs to this tradition of kitchen cosmetics.

paras: Early natural lip colours included ochre, red lac with beeswax, and plant stains in beeswax.[1] Petal stains follow the same principle using flowers at hand.
